title: Use a substitution
text: Let $$u=3\theta.$$ First, find the general solution for the simpler equation $$\tan(u)=\sqrt{3}.$$

title: Find the general solution for u
text: The reference angle where tangent equals $$\sqrt{3}$$ is $$\frac{\pi}{3}.$$ Since the tangent function has a period of $$\pi, $$ the general solution for $$u$$ is $$u=\frac{\pi}{3}+n\pi.$$

title: Substitute back
text: Now substitute $$3\theta$$ back in for $$u$$ to get $$3\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}+n\pi.$$

title: Isolate theta
text: To solve for $$\theta$$ you must divide the entire equation by $$3$$. Be careful to divide both the reference angle AND the period term.
